TITLE: SCULPT for Accessibility | Worcestershire County Council

DESCRIPTION: SCULPT for Accessibility is a beginners guide to raise basic awareness and skills for accessibility across the wider workforce.

HEADINGS: SCULPT for Accessibility | What is SCULPT? | SCULPT at Worcestershire County Council | SCULPT can be adopted by anyone | Tell us your SCULPT story | SCULPT license | Useful links

CONTENT: In this section Digital project showcase Our Information Governance Strategy Our Digital Accessibility Strategy Geographic Information System Maps SCULPT for Accessibility Digital accessibility information for our third party providers (DRAFT) Digital, Data and Technology Strategy Artificial Intelligence (AI) Domain registration SCULPT training example Digital help SCULPT at the Intellectual Property Office (IPO) case study SCULPT for Accessibility SCULPT for Accessibility SCULPT for Accessibility is a beginners guide to raise basic awareness and skills for accessibility across the wider workforce. What is SCULPT? SCULPT came out of research to understand user needs and to address basic digital accessibility awareness and training requirements for a wider workforce approach. The full journey to develop SCULPT can be read at AbilityNet Everyone can SCULPT for Accessibility . SCULPT is a simple acronym and underlying framework to introduce the basic principles of digital accessibility in a bite-sized approachable way. Using feedback, we have added to the original SCULPT model to cater for a much broader range of digital content beyond just documents. SCULPT now stands for: S stands for structuring a document using headings C stands for colour contrast , colour use , captions and checkers for accessibility U is use of images and alt text L refers to links and logical reading order P is plain language T stands for tables, text and transcripts SCULPT at Worcestershire County Council This is how we use sculpt in our organisation: mandatory e-learning module for all new starters and existing staff to underpin basic awareness of digital accessibility and the SCULPT principles SCULPT support area on our intranet with on-demand resources specific to each principle of SCULPT to assist staff in their everyday practice. bespoke learning sessions can be requested for service areas internally based on their specific needs. See an example of some lunch and learn SCULPT sessions from the SEND and Alternative Provision Partnership Committee SCULPT also forms part of our Digital Accessibility Strategy and is embedded within our Equality, Diversity and Inclusion Strategy (PDF) . SCULPT can be adopted by anyone We see SCULPT as a simple way to communicate some basic principles of digital accessibility and a starting point to shape inclusive practices. It was a finalist in four national awards during 2021 and 2022, including the AbilityNet Tech4Good Awards . Anyone can use the SCULPT acronym to develop their own approach to digital accessibility. To get you started our posters and logos are free to download. SCULPT has been acknowledged nationally: SCULPT for Accessibility Government Communication Service SCULPT DWP Accessibility Manual Additionally, many other organisations have adopted and shared the SCULPT model, here are a small cross-section of examples: SCULPT for Accessibility University of Reading Accessible documents Cambridgeshire County Council SCULPT for Accessibility Somerset NHS Foundation Trust SCULPT framework SportScotland Tell us your SCULPT story Over the years we've had many organisations contact us about how we embedded SCULPT at Worcestershire County Council. In addition, we've also had organisations tell us how they've adopted and then creatively adapted SCULPT to fit their specific organisational needs. No organisation is the same, so we are asking those who have adopted SCULPT to tell us their story so as a community we can inspire others to follow our lead. Tell us about your SCULPT adoption SCULPT license SCULPT by Helen Wilson is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International Licence . Based on work at Worcestershire County Council. A Creative Commons license means that SCULPT is free to adopt, all that we ask is that you acknowledge us by pointing back to this webpage if you use it. chunks.mini_summary:
- SCULPT for Accessibility is a beginners guide to raise basic awareness and skills for accessibility across the wider workforce.
- SCULPT stands for: S - structuring documents, C - colour contrast & use, U - images with alt text, L - links in logical order, P - plain language, T - tables and transcripts.
- Worcestershire County Council uses SCULPT as a mandatory e-learning module for new starters and existing staff.
- SCULPT forms part of Worcestershire County Council's Digital Accessibility Strategy and Equality, Diversity and Inclusion Strategy.
- SCULPT is free to adopt with the request to acknowledge Worcestershire County Council by pointing back to this webpage.
- Many other organisations have adopted SCULPT, including examples from the University of Reading, Cambridgeshire County Council, and Somerset NHS Foundation Trust.

CONTENT: An update on One Worcestershire. As part of our evolving strategic direction, One Worcestershire, which was established nearly 10 years ago ahead of the growth of Visit Worcestershire and the Worcestershire Growth Hub, is being integrated into the county’s wider investment and showcasing support platforms. This transition reflects our commitment to a more streamlined and collaborative approach that aligns with Worcestershire’s broader ambitions for investment, growth, and economic development. While the One Worcestershire name will no longer be used in this space, its values, partnerships, and legacy will continue to shape how we promote Worcestershire and champion opportunities across the region. For information on travel, tourism and visitor opportunities, please visit: www.visitworcestershire.org . Email: visitworcestershire@worcestershire.gov.uk . Investment and Business Support For investment, business growth and support services, please visit: www.worcestershiregrowthhub.co.uk . Email: info@worcestershiregrowthhub.co.uk . - The Equality Act 2010 consolidates existing discrimination laws into one piece of legislation covering employment, services, and goods.
- Worcestershire County Council has a devolved model for equality, diversity, and inclusion work with Equality Champions in each service area.
- The Council has a governance structure including Directorate Equality Groups (DEG) and a Strategic Diversity Leadership Group (SDLG) to ensure fair decisions and progress.
- Regular reporting on EDI progress is conducted quarterly at the DEG level and annually for publication.
- Objectives include building an empowered community, embedding EDI at all levels, ensuring fair measures, and empowering employees.
- Measures to achieve these objectives include engaging communities, supporting training and employment initiatives, collaborating with partners, monitoring staff satisfaction, and providing EDI training.
- The Council aims to attract diverse talent by removing barriers in recruitment, developing a positive action plan, and analyzing workforce data.
- Communications are designed to promote inclusion and belonging, celebrating the diverse current and potential workforce.

chunks.mini_summary:
- Use headings and subheadings to structure your document.
- Employ colours effectively to enhance readability without causing contrast issues.
- Provide alt text for all images to ensure they are accessible to visually impaired users.
- Describe your links fully using clear, understandable text instead of phrases like "click here".
- Create tables with clear formats, avoiding merged cells, to ensure accessibility.
- Use simple language and avoid jargon to improve document comprehension.

tags.summary: SCULPT for Accessibility is a comprehensive guide developed by Worcestershire County Council to enhance digital accessibility across the workforce. It covers key principles such as structuring documents, using appropriate color contrast, employing alt text for images, ensuring logical link order, writing in plain language, and managing table structures and transcripts. The guide is free to use with attribution and has been adopted by various organizations including Worcestershire County Council itself, the University of Reading, Cambridgeshire County Council, and Somerset NHS Foundation Trust. It serves as a mandatory e-learning module for new starters and existing staff within Worcestershire County Council, promoting equality, diversity, and inclusion through digital accessibility practices.
tags.rationale: The primary tags were justified based on explicit mentions in the summaries: 'SCULPT for Accessibility is a beginners guide to raise basic awareness and skills for accessibility across the wider workforce' (Section 1 summary), indicating an educational focus. mini_summaries:
- SCULPT for Accessibility is a beginners guide to raise basic awareness and skills for accessibility across the wider workforce.
- SCULPT stands for: S - structuring documents, C - colour contrast & use, U - images with alt text, L - links in logical order, P - plain language, T - tables and transcripts.
- Worcestershire County Council uses SCULPT as a mandatory e-learning module for new starters and existing staff.
- SCULPT forms part of Worcestershire County Council's Digital Accessibility Strategy and Equality, Diversity and Inclusion Strategy.
- SCULPT is free to adopt with the request to acknowledge Worcestershire County Council by pointing back to this webpage.
- Many other organisations have adopted SCULPT, including examples from the University of Reading, Cambridgeshire County Council, and Somerset NHS Foundation Trust.

- SCULPT is an acronym for digital accessibility concepts: Structure, Colour and contrast, Use of images, Links (hyperlinks), Plain English, Table structure.
- Worcestershire County Council maintains the SCULPT guidance for creating accessible documents.
- For web accessibility, check against the tips outlined in the SCULPT documentation to avoid introducing accessibility issues.
- SCULPT is developed within Higher Education but valuable for anyone aiming to enhance website accessibility.
- The SCULPT framework is used by various organizations, including Worcestershire County Council, the University of Reading, Somerset NHS Foundation Trust, and sportscotland.
- SCULPT by Helen Wilson is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International License, allowing for its use and modification as long as it's attributed and shared under similar terms.

- Prioritise and embed Equality, Diversity and Inclusion (EDI) at all levels of the organization.
- Engage and encourage participation between different communities within the organization.
- Ensure visible senior leadership in driving EDI initiatives.
- Encourage colleagues to contribute and collaborate in advancing EDI.
- Implement a governance structure for EDI with clear responsibilities.
- Provide proactive future-proofing opportunities for underrepresented groups.
- Use communications to promote inclusion and a sense of belonging among all employees.

- The Equality Act 2010 consolidates existing discrimination laws into one piece of legislation covering employment, services, and goods.
- Worcestershire County Council has a devolved model for equality, diversity, and inclusion work with Equality Champions in each service area.
- The Council has a governance structure including Directorate Equality Groups (DEG) and a Strategic Diversity Leadership Group (SDLG) to ensure fair decisions and progress.
- Regular reporting on EDI progress is conducted quarterly at the DEG level and annually for publication.
- Objectives include building an empowered community, embedding EDI at all levels, ensuring fair measures, and empowering employees.
- Measures to achieve these objectives include engaging communities, supporting training and employment initiatives, collaborating with partners, monitoring staff satisfaction, and providing EDI training.
- The Council aims to attract diverse talent by removing barriers in recruitment, developing a positive action plan, and analyzing workforce data.
- Communications are designed to promote inclusion and belonging, celebrating the diverse current and potential workforce.

- Use headings and subheadings to structure your document.
- Employ colours effectively to enhance readability without causing contrast issues.
- Provide alt text for all images to ensure they are accessible to visually impaired users.
- Describe your links fully using clear, understandable text instead of phrases like "click here".
- Create tables with clear formats, avoiding merged cells, to ensure accessibility.
- Use simple language and avoid jargon to improve document comprehension.
